what:
THE CHECKLIST VOCABULARY GUARD DOES NOT READ THE `lane` FIELD AT ALL, so it cannot catch the exact condition the close-out skill's check 3 tells every session to verify by hand: 'No row says in_flight if nobody is working it. Check this explicitly -- a stale in_flight tells the next session a lane is live when it is not, and it will route around work that is actually free.'
MEASURED 2026-09-24 with a positive control, because a grep that finds nothing proves nothing on its own: `grep -c lane` over scripts/ci/check_manager_checklist_vocabulary.py returns 0 (exit 1), while `grep -c '"state"'` over the same file returns 6 (exit 0). So the probe can find a field the guard reads, and `lane` is genuinely absent. The guard's own success line -- 'every item's effective state is unambiguous and every declared value is in the file's own vocabulary' -- is about the state VOCABULARY, not about state/lane coherence, and reading its green as coverage of this is the negative-with-no-denominator error.
LIVE INSTANCES TODAY, and both are BENIGN, which is why this is severity low rather than high: E27 (state queued, lane session_01HD2geAyqSQQu66Ah7wb8sU) and E34 (state queued, lane session_01N43beYx4nnvdoy8BjWtr1W). Both notes explain that the lane is archived and pushed no PR, and E27's note explicitly cites close-out check 3 as the reason it was reset to `queued`. So a session DID do this correctly by hand. That is the point: it worked because someone remembered, not because anything checks.
WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW AT ALL, given this repo's stated allergy to filing: the cost of the miss is asymmetric and silent. A row reading `in_flight` or carrying a live-looking lane makes the NEXT manager route around work that is actually free -- the failure is invisible at the moment it happens and shows up as a lane that never got dispatched. Close-out check 3 exists because this already happened; it is currently defended by instruction only.
[!] WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any OTHER guard covers this. Only check_manager_checklist_vocabulary.py was inspected -- check_manager_scope.py and check_manager_queue_watch.py were not read for `lane` handling. Confirming or ruling those out is the first step of the work, not a conclusion of this row.
